question: Eight times the present age of P exceeds the present age of Q by 46 years. After 10 years, three times Q’s age will be 12 years less than eight times P’s age at that time. What is the present age (in years) of Q?
solution:
**Given:**

Eight times P’s age exceeds Q’s age by 46 years.

After 10 years, three times Q’s age will be 12 years less than eight times P’s age.

**Formula Used:**

Future age = Present age + years

Linear equations solved by substitution

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let present ages be P and Q.

⇒ 8P − Q = 46 …(1)

⇒ After 10 years: 3(Q + 10) = 8(P + 10) − 12 …(2)

⇒ Expand equation (2):

⇒ 3Q + 30 = 8P + 80 − 12

⇒ 3Q = 8P + 38 …(3)

⇒ From (1): Q = 8P − 46

⇒ Substitute into (3):

⇒ 3(8P − 46) = 8P + 38

⇒ 24P − 138 = 8P + 38

⇒ 24P − 8P = 176

⇒ 16P = 176

⇒ P = 11

⇒ Q = 8P − 46

⇒ Q = 88 − 46

⇒ Q = 42

**∴ The present age of Q is 42 years.**
